title: Iteration-counts Lemma case (L): 'bounded factor absorbed into O(1)' not proved

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Rigor gap in 'Iteration counts' Lemma case (L)** (used for Fibonacci (c) and Lucas (d)).

Case (L) asserts: if $N(x)\asymp\log_b x$ up to a bounded multiplicative factor in $[\tfrac12,2]$, then $T(n)=\log^*_b n+O(1)$, claiming the distortion 'can be absorbed' by comparing $x\mapsto\tfrac12\log_b x$ and $x\mapsto2\log_b x$.

This is not proven. A constant multiplicative factor *inside an iterated logarithm* does not obviously change the $\log^*$ count by only an additive $O(1)$; the effect near the bottom of the tower must be tracked explicitly. One must prove that for $c\in[\tfrac12,2]$ the iteration count of $x\mapsto c\log_b x$ differs from $\log^*_b n$ by a bounded amount, e.g. by induction on tower height with explicit interval bookkeeping.

Empirically the Fibonacci $k(n)$ sits a *bounded* additive amount (~3, partly from $M=3$) below $\log^*_\varphi n$, so the final claim $k\sim\log^*_\varphi n$ is plausibly correct (since $\log^*\to\infty$), but the lemma as written does not establish it. Note the convergence is extremely slow: at $n=10^{200}$, $k(n)=5$ while $\log^*_\varphi n=8$.
